newsitem.title: UK: Elf loads first cargo of LPG from Congo's Nkossa. [CORRECTED 00:53 GMT 29/1]
newsitem.headline: Elf loads first cargo of LPG from Congo's Nkossa. [CORRECTED 00:53 GMT 29/1]

text.p: The first cargo of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) has been lifted from Elf's deep water offshore Nkossa field in the Congo, a statement from Elf Aquitaine said on Tuesday.
"The first lifting of LPG...has just been effected on schedule," the statement said. A vessel had already loaded 3,500 tonnes of butane and was destined for Abidjan and Dakar, it added.
The module which treats the LPG has a capacity of 1,300 tonnes of LPG per day, and total LPG output should be more than 350,000 tonnes this year, rising to over 500,000 tonnes in 1998.
Half of the output will be propane and half will be butane, the statement said.
Nkossa currently produces crude oil at a rate of 100,000 (corrects from 80,000) barrels per day (bpd.).

The Nkossa field lies in 170 metres of water and is operated by Elf Congo, with a 51 percent stake. Other partners are Chevron Overseas (Congo) Ltd with 30 percent, Hydro-Congo with 15 percent, and Energy Africa Haute Mer Ltd Ltd with four percent (Corrects final company name).
